newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo in alliance with baseball league.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo in alliance with baseball league.

text.p: Pepsi-Cola Co., contending baseball is seeing a resurgence in popularity among fans recently disgruntled over labour strife, said Wednesday it has entered into a five-year marketing alliance with Major League Baseball.

The soft drink maker, which has similar deals with Major League Soccer and the NASCAR stock car racing association, plans to spend more than $50 million over the five-year period covered by the deal on advertising and other promotional efforts linked to baseball.

"When you look at sports properties, particularly those that might be underleveraged, baseball pops to the top," Pepsi spokesman Brad Shaw said. "We think baseball has turned the corner. We think it's really on the verge of a renaissance."
Under terms of the deal, Pepsi and Major League Baseball are developing a joint logo to be called: "Pepsi, the choice of Major League Baseball."

Pepsi also will have exclusive rights to baseball's All-Star balloting. Pepsi will tie in with 6,000 7-11 convenience stores to display the All-Star ballots along with displays of their soft drink products.
In addition, computer users who tap into Pepsi's World Wide Web site (http://www.pepsi.com) will be able to cast an All-Star ballot, Shaw said.

The company also plans to offer baseball-related products, such as T-shirts and caps, as part of its annual "Pepsi Stuff" promotion, which allows consumers to collect points that can be redeemed for Pepsi promotional products.
The company said the alliance would not prevent stadiums from continuing to sell soft drinks from its chief rival, Coca-Cola Co.
